title: Semi-Cliffordness of the Clifford hierarchy for a single qudit in composite dimensions
abstract: An important question in quantum information theory asks whether every gate in the Clifford hierarchy is semi-Clifford or not, as such gates admit resource-efficient implementations via gate teleportation. Extending recent results for prime dimensions~\cite{silva_clifford_2025}, we prove that every hierarchy gate on a single qudit of dimension \(d\) is semi-Clifford, if and only if \(d\) is square-free. In composite dimensions, \(\mathbb{Z}_d^2\) is a symplectic module rather than a vector space, motivating a distinction between four types of gates. Semi-Clifford gates ($\mathcal{SC}$) are the ones that become diagonal under left and right multiplication by Clifford gates, while a broader class $\mathcal{N}$ admits a permutation diagonal form, under left and right multiplication by Cliffords. Lagrangian semi-Clifford gates ($\mathcal{LSC}$) conjugate some maximal abelian Pauli subgroup to another, whereas generalized semi-Clifford gates ($\mathcal{GSC}$) map some maximal abelian Pauli subalgebra to another under conjugation. In square-free dimensions, we have \(\mathcal{SC}=\mathcal{LSC}\) and \(\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{GSC}\), but when \(d\) is not square-free, these equivalences can fail, as Lagrangian submodules can become non-free. We also show that every third-level gate of the one-qudit Clifford hierarchy is a generalized semi-Clifford in arbitrary dimensions.
summary: This paper characterizes when all gates in the Clifford hierarchy for a single qudit are semi-Clifford, proving this holds if and only if the qudit dimension $d$ is square-free. It develops sophisticated mathematical tools using module theory to distinguish between various gate classes ($	ext{SC}, 	ext{LSC}, 	ext{N}, 	ext{GSC}$) in composite dimensions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the necessary and sufficient conditions for all gates in the Clifford hierarchy of a single qudit to be semi-Clifford, particularly when the qudit dimension $d$ is composite.
main_result: The hierarchy gates are semi-Clifford if and only if the dimension $d$ is square-free; otherwise, various structural equivalences between gate classes (SC, LSC, N, GSC) fail.
method: The authors extend results from prime dimensions to composite dimensions using advanced ring-theoretic tools, module theory over $\mathbb{Z}_d$, and analysis of symplectic modules.
model_or_system: The system is a single qudit of dimension $d$, whose underlying mathematical structure is analyzed using the symplectic module $\mathbb{Z}_d^2$. The analysis involves classifying various types of quantum gates (Clifford, Semi-Clifford, etc.).
key_observables: The membership of gates in different structural classes ($	ext{SC}, 	ext{LSC}, 	ext{N}, 	ext{GSC}$) and the square-free nature of the dimension $d$.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ (especially its prime factorization), and the level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy ($C_k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis requires using ring-theoretic substitutes for vector-space methods, which is necessary when $d$ is composite.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the relationships between the four types of gates ($	ext{SC}, 	ext{N}, 	ext{LSC}, 	ext{GSC}$) across different dimensions and hierarchy levels.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the main theorem relating semi-Clifford property to square-free dimensions. It then delves into the mathematical machinery by analyzing Lagrangian submodules of the symplectic module $\mathbb{Z}_{2p^\alpha}^2$ to support the structural claims regarding gate equivalences.
why_interesting: The work provides deep structural constraints on quantum gates, which is fundamental for understanding resource-efficient quantum computation protocols like gate teleportation.
